court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Anil Yashwant Karande vs Smt. Mangal Anil Karande
facts_of_case: The parties were married in 2002. The respondent was forced to leave the matrimonial house and an FIR was lodged against the appellant under various IPC sections. The respondent filed a petition for restitution of conjugal rights. The trial court granted reliefs in favour of the respondent.

legal_principles.principle: A respondent is entitled to maintain a petition for restitution of conjugal rights independently, even if they have committed any cruelty upon the other party.
legal_principles.held: He submits that even if this Court comes to the conclusion that any cruelty was committed by the respondent upon the appellant, this Court cannot set aside the orders passed by the two Courts below insofar as the reliefs of restitution of conjugal rights under section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act has been granted in favor of the respondent is concerned.

legal_principles.principle: A court cannot set aside the orders passed by lower courts in a case, unless there is a substantial question of law involved.
legal_principles.held: He submits that the judgments delivered under family court appeal cannot be relied upon since in family court appeal, the Court has to consider all the questions of facts and law whereas in the second appeal, the Court can interfere only if substantial question of law arises.

outcome.final_order: The appeal was allowed and the order passed by the lower appellate bench granting reliefs to the respondent was set aside.
